source.title: First-Passage Prediction of Grokking Delay: ACalibrated Law under AdamW with Causal Validation
source.authors: Xuan Khanh Truong; Truong Quynh Hoa; Trung Duc Luu; D. Phan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests delayed generalization on algorithmic tasks, but focuses on norm and angular trajectories, interventions, and a delay-prediction law rather than reproducing the original study's full recipe.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own accuracy transitions, delay predictions, norm/angular measurements, and causal interventions. Literature results cited by the paper, including claims about Fourier circuits in other work, are not rows. The paper does not directly test whether shrinking the training set increases delay.
record.test_reason: The paper trains small models on modular arithmetic and sparse parity under AdamW and reports when train and validation accuracy cross 0.99. This is a different method aimed at the same delayed-generalisation question, not a replication of the original recipe. It adds weight-decay and norm interventions that bear on the low-norm-bias part of V5, and continuous norm and angle measures that bear on the progress-measure part of V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that, on algorithmic tasks under AdamW, grokking delay is a joint crossing of norm contraction and angular displacement. It is predictable by a calibrated first-passage law (MAPE 17.7–23.3%). Block F shows weight-decay-driven contraction is causally necessary, and magnitude alone (F2 rescale) is not sufficient. They note that κ is measured empirically, not derived, and that scope is limited to algorithmic tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular algorithmic tasks and train/validation accuracy to study delayed generalization, but adds AdamW-specific norm and angular measurements, causal interventions, and a calibrated first-passage prediction law. The paper does not present itself as an explicit replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome and measured transition timing depend on task and architecture; the paper reports immediate generalization on sparse parity, task-scale variation across p, and sensitivity of the 2-layer results to the validation threshold (0.95 versus 0.99). The paper also reports cross-cell variation in angular thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: A closed-form first-passage law calibrated on one cell predicts held-out grokking delay with MAPE 17.7%, 18.0% and 23.3% across three tiers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under AdamW, grokking delay ≈ log(Vmem/V*)/(2κηλ), with κ an architecture-level constant.

fits_no_version.finding: Rescaling parameters by 0.9 at Tmem does not shorten the delay, which the authors read as magnitude alone being insufficient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking requires a joint norm–angle crossing; instant norm reduction does not speed it up.

record.problems: Causal Block F conditions have N = 3 each; the authors describe the rescale result as a weak test with a wide confidence interval. Empirical scope is algorithmic tasks, and the study does not directly vary training fraction to test the claimed training-set-size delay trend. The angular theorem relies on local linearization assumptions and empirical calibration.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-cell κ estimates, κ decomposition, and optimizer-architecture comparisons were not extracted because they measure contraction-rate corrections rather than the claim's accuracy transition or the versions' named circuit-efficiency and artifact effects. Cited findings from other papers were excluded.

untested.parts: Training fraction is fixed at 0.4, so the delay-vs-training-set-size trend is not isolated. The p-sweep changes absolute set size but is confounded with task size.
No circuit (e.g. Fourier) identification, and no measure of memorising components being removed.
Untested: no non-algorithmic data, and no initialisation-scale or lazy-to-rich manipulation.
Untested: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Untested: selection of a more efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Untested: learned algorithms are not compared across runs.
Untested: no control of floating-point or softmax effects or of adaptive-optimizer instabilities. The SGD comparison fails before memorisation.

missing.what: Median Tgrok rises as p falls: p=53 8,100; p=67 4,800; p=89 2,900; p=113 2,600 steps, at a fixed 40% train fraction. Smaller absolute training sets (about 1,124 at p=53) take longer, but the effect is confounded with task size.
missing.locator: Appendix G.3, Table 2; G.6 'Failure mode at small p'

missing.what: λ=0.01 does not grok within 50k steps. Delay scales roughly as 1/λ (λ-exponent 1.26 ± 0.21), and very large λ prevents memorisation.
Vanilla SGD at the same hyperparameters never memorises (train accuracy 1.9%), while AdamW groks 3/3.
missing.versions: V7 (context only; not a test of the artifact claim)

record.verdict_notes: Block F has N=3 per condition. The V2 link is weak because the progress measures are norm and angle, not circuits; a researcher may prefer to treat r2 and r8 as fits_no_version. The paper mentions Fourier circuits only interpretively, with no measurement. The Figure 2 caption's pooled median (0.268) conflicts with its panel label (0.242).

versions.untested_parts: The paper varies modulus and task scale, but does not directly isolate training-set size or report whether a smaller training set requires more optimization.
It measures norm and angular trajectories, not the formation of an identified generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or Fourier-circuit progress.
Non-algorithmic data and initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich interventions are not tested.
LLM pretraining and realistic-data fine-tuning are not tested.
The interventions test weight-decay-driven contraction and norm freezing, but not whether a more efficient circuit is selected, a critical dataset size exists, or ungrokking occurs below it.
The paper does not identify and compare algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts under controlled numerical settings.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Rescale all parameters by 0.9 while preserving optimizer moments.
rows.note: The authors say the interval rules out only changes of approximately 30% or greater; the result is not a sharp test.
rows.check: A 0.9x rescale tests the paper's own magnitude-only reading of its law; V5 makes no prediction about instant rescaling. CI [−353, +419] at N=3 is uninformative.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: After the trigger, project parameters after each gradient step to keep Vt fixed at VTmem.
rows.measure: Grokking outcome and final angular distance
rows.note: The paper reports that the projection kept Vt constant to numerical precision.
rows.check: Holding the norm fixed tests the low-norm bias in V5. The V5 prediction (no generalisation without norm reduction) is observed, so the state should be observed, not absent. V1 and V2 links removed: the row is an intervention, not a circuit-formation or baseline-delay measure.

source_check.locator_found: Section 6.5; Appendix E.6, F3 norm-freeze; Appendix E.10.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Set the optimizer weight_decay parameter to 0 after the trigger.
rows.measure: Grokking outcome and final angular distance
rows.note: The authors interpret F3 and F4 as evidence that weight-decay-driven contraction is causally necessary in this setting.
rows.check: Removing weight decay at Tmem stops grokking (0/3), as V5 predicts, so the state should be observed, not absent. V1 and V2 links removed for the same reason as r5.

rows.subject: models across Block H
rows.operation_detail: Track angular distance from the Tmem parameters and compare it with the cell-specific critical angle.

conditions.value: 12 cells across architecture, η, λ, p, and task; 3 seeds per cell

rows.measure: Angular threshold and whether trajectories cross it before grokking
rows.value: All 36 runs grokked and all 36 crossed their cell-specific α⋆ before Tgrok; cross-cell mean α⋆ = 52.8° ± 7.9° (CV 15.0%).
rows.note: The paper says Block H supports consistency but does not directly test angular necessity, because it has no angular-trapping intervention.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix J, sweep dimensions, outcomes, Table 3 and implications for Theorem 1.

rows.subject: paper's 2-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compare validation-transition timing at 0.95 and 0.99 accuracy thresholds.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± 528 steps at the 0.95 threshold; CV 18%
rows.note: The paper attributes the later 0.99 crossings to post-grokking oscillations and overshoot, not a distinct contraction phase.
rows.check: All 29 seeds grok after memorisation. Only the 0.99-threshold timing is bimodal because of post-grok overshoot. The effect is present, so observed rather than partial; the threshold dependence goes into the label.
